rel_raw: During the past 150 years, the box–ironbark ecosystem has been severely fragmented by agricultural clearing and degraded by mining and overharvesting of timber and firewood (Traill, 1993, Calder, Calder and McCann, 1994). About 85% of the original ecosystem has been cleared, with the most extensive losses being among the moister woodlands on fertile alluvial soils surrounding the remnant foothill habitats and extending onto the northern plains (ECC, 1997). Much of the remaining area was intensively harvested during the initial gold-mining era.
